cases.situation: My college roommate Sophie's mom died. We haven't talked in a couple of years, but I knew her mom, she used to send us care packages with lemon bars during finals.
cases.reply: Sophie, I'm so sorry about your mom. I still think about those lemon bars showing up every finals week, she fed half our floor. Thinking of you and your dad. No need to reply to this.
cases.note: A years-long gap doesn't need explaining; the specific memory is what she'll keep.

cases.situation: 我手下的员工小李，父亲昨天去世了，他已经请假回老家。我想以领导的身份给他发个微信。
cases.reply: 小李，听说你父亲去世了，非常难过。工作的事一点都不用操心，你手上的项目我已经安排小周接着跟。需要休多久就休多久。想着你和家人，不用回复。
cases.note: 作为领导，最具体的帮助就是把工作接过去，并且明说不用回复。

cases.situation: My best friend Marco's wife Elena died a year ago this Saturday. I want to text him something that day.
cases.reply: Thinking about you and Elena today. I still smile about her making us redo the barbecue because we'd 'insulted the ribs'. I'm around all weekend if you want company. No need to reply.
cases.note: The anniversary message matters more than the first one, because most people have stopped sending them.

cases.situation: 好朋友阿杰的爸爸三周前去世了。我这几周隔几天就发消息问他怎么样，昨天他回我：我没事，别老问了。我有点慌，不知道还要不要再联系他。
cases.reply: 好，我不追着问了。我在，不会走开。周六下午我把你爱吃的老街卤味挂你家门把手上，不用开门，也不用回我。
cases.note: 被推开时不辩解也不消失：接受他的话，把“问候”换成不需要回应的陪伴。之后隔一两周发一句，不带问题。
